# Desktop games

LÖVE, Pygame and native Bevy games run in desktop windows, outside the preview pane.
Defold builds outside its editor with Bob (Java); GameMaker CLI builds need Igor,
its installed runtime and licence setup. Neither toolchain is bundled with Voyager.

A Godot game uses Voyager's pinned engine and commands; read [godot.md](godot.md) before changing its code, assets or tests.

A rigged 3D character with clothes or several body types follows blender's
[rigged characters](../../blender/references/game-characters.md) guide.
Test with a [Godot-only playtest](godot.md#playtests); a changed source revision needs retesting.

# Godot

`voyager godot --help` lists the commands; `voyager godot start --help` shows
operations, flags and the scenario file shape. Use Voyager's pinned engine
(`godot status`, `godot setup`), never a Godot found on PATH. Start a new game with
`godot create` in an empty folder; the starters are editable, so read their scripts.

## Assets

`godot start --operation asset --asset '{…}'` converts a source into a validated,
cached project asset (model→GLB, image→PNG, audio→Ogg Vorbis, cinematic→Theora) and
lists it in `game-assets.json`. Fields: `id` (lowercase slug), `source`, `kind`
(`model|image|audio|cinematic`), `provenance` (where it came from), `dependencies`
(include a .blend's linked libraries), `width`/`height` (image size), `loop` (audio),
`maxTriangles`, `maxMaterials`, `maxDimension`, `requiredAnimations`, `pivot`
(`center`/`base` check the origin; they do not move it), `collisionHint` (metadata
only; add collision shapes yourself), `transparency` (`required|opaque|preserve`),
`preview` (model/image render; needs a display), `style`, `blender`. Game code loads
them with `preload("res://game_assets.gd").get_asset(id)`, which applies `loop`.
Importing files into `res://` directly also works.

## Playtests

`godot start --operation test --scenario file.json` runs the main scene under a
development runner that sends real input events. Each step holds one key, action or
mouse input for `frames`; a step without input waits. `expect` checks `snapshot()`
fields after the step; `until` ends the step when they match and fails if `frames`
run out; `assert` checks a node property (`scope: "node"`) or snapshot field
(`"state"`); `invariants` are checked every tick. Screenshots need `rendered: true`;
`recording: true` also writes an AVI (at most 36,000 requested frames). Results are in the job's `report.json`.

The main scene can provide these; they are plain game code and ship in exports:

```gdscript
signal gameplay_event(event_name: String, data: Dictionary)  # JSON-compatible data
func snapshot() -> Dictionary                # state scenarios check
func objectives() -> Array[Dictionary]       # {id, label, progress, required, complete}
func interactables() -> Array[Dictionary]    # {id, label, node, available}
var save_path                                # runner points it at a per-run file
```

Game logic must not detect the runner, and tests never read the user's real saves.

# Browser games

For someone new to game-making, Phaser (2D) and three.js (3D) cover
most browser games. Voyager also supports PixiJS, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas and
KAPLAY; any can be the better fit for what the user wants.

Know:

- The
  handoff also opens by double-click: one self-contained HTML file (vite-plugin-singlefile).
- Open it in the preview pane with `preview_open` on the dev server's URL. Play it with
  `preview_click` and `preview_press`, look with `preview_snapshot`, and read state with
  `preview_evaluate`; exposing the game object on `window` makes that easy.
  `preview_recording_start` captures a gameplay clip.
- Voyager publication uses a readable game slug plus an automatic six-character random suffix,
  such as `moon-hop-a2b3c4.voyager.site`. Follow publish-game to choose the slug on first release.
- Any website can iframe a public Voyager game using its root URL plus `?embed=1`; follow
  publish-game's embed example. Embedding does not provide a privileged Voyager bridge or
  relax the game's sandbox and static hosting restrictions.
- Voyager hosts built static output: bundle assets locally, and do not promise shared live rooms
  or an external game server on voyager.site. Shared rooms need the user's own server and a host
  that permits its connections. Free Voyager accounts allow two live games. Free, Starter, and
  accounts without a plan receive a quick, permissive AI safety check that fails open on a
  model outage or timeout. Plans above Starter skip content checks; structural bundle validation
  applies to every plan.

# Playable X games Build: - One HTTPS origin serving the share page, which is itself the full game. **Implement and test `?embed=1`** on the same page: it fills the iframe without page chrome. Voyager's player URL is always the stable root plus `?embed=1`; Studio supplies the title, poster, player tags, 480×480 dimensions and headers permitting embedding on any site, including X. Do not invent player options or dimensions in the upload manifest. - The frame is sandboxed: never use `
` (submission is blocked), `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt`. In embed mode a corner "Open full game ↗" link opens the share page without `embed=1` (on Voyager the stable root `/`; a shared room's own `/r/`) with `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and the `embed=1` flag survives any in-game navigation. - **Require a square PNG/JPEG/WebP poster** showing gameplay, the game title and **"Tap to play"**, made with make-image or captured from the game. Include it in the built folder and pass `--thumbnail-path poster.png` to both prepare and publish. Voyager versions the hosted asset URL when publishing updates; keep sharing the stable root URL. Follow [browser games](web.md) for the build loop (Vite with `base: './'`, the preview tools, sprites, sound and music). For a requested public release, follow [publish-game](../../publish-game/SKILL.md) and share its root URL. Follow that skill's limit/refusal handling. # X player card for a game ## Voyager publishing Use [publish-game](../../publish-game/SKILL.md) for a requested public release. Voyager is the default host, using the existing account and a permanent `https://-.voyager.site` root URL. An X release **requires a square PNG/JPEG/WebP poster with the title and "Tap to play"**. Include it in the built folder, then pass `--thumbnail-path poster.png` to both prepare and publish. Studio supplies `twitter:card=player`, the stable root plus `?embed=1` as `twitter:player`, and width/height `480`. It escapes the title, versions the poster URL, and supplies headers permitting any site to frame the game. Inspect the emitted `twitter:image` instead of guessing its storage path. The upload manifest still contains only `schema_version`, `entrypoint`, optional `thumbnail_path` and `files`. Do not add player URL or dimension fields. General publishing can omit the thumbnail, with the warning **X will show a plain link card, not the playable game**; the X game workflow requires it. X decides actual inline playback, so the complete game must work in a browser too. ## Layout Implement `?embed=1` on the same page, filling the square without page chrome. Keep all controls, score and restart in the frame. Test this mode and the full browser game. For Voyager, build `index.html`, the required poster, and local assets; do not add host configuration files. `index.html?embed=1` is the player URL. The page reads the flag to drop page chrome and show "Open full game ↗". On Voyager the link targets the stable root, never the versioned `/_v/…` document it redirects to: ```html Open full game ↗ ``` ## Framing headers Voyager permits embedding on any site, including X. It owns these headers; verify the final player response has no restrictive `frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options` header. Do not try to change Voyager hosting restrictions with a bundled `_headers` file or meta tag. For the user's own host, an equivalent unrestricted framing policy is: ``` Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors * ``` The share page must send no `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`, or `unsafe-none`: the new tab inherits X's frame sandbox, and Chromium blocks any other value with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE`. ## Shared rooms Voyager's hosting is static and blocks external network connections. It cannot host shared rooms, even when their client builds successfully. Shared play needs the user's own server and hosting/security policy that allows its connections. Cloudflare Pages alone is static too; a Worker/Durable Object or another server is a separate deployment requiring user intent.

For someone new to
game-making, Phaser (2D in the browser), three.js (3D in the browser) and Godot
(desktop 2D or 3D) cover most games. Unity or Unreal suit teams already using them.
Voyager also supports PixiJS, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas, KAPLAY, LÖVE, Pygame, Bevy,
Defold and GameMaker (plus Unity, Unreal and Roblox); any can be the better fit
for what the user wants. Use `unity-engine` for Unity, `unreal-engine` for Unreal,
`roblox-studio` for Roblox.

Build a complete start, play, win-or-lose and restart loop. Playtest through real input; a changed source revision needs retesting.

Read the target guide before building or changing the game:

- [Desktop games](references/desktop.md), including the pinned Godot commands and playtests.
- [Browser games](references/web.md), including the preview tools and static bundle contract.
- [Playable X games](references/x-player-card.md), plus the browser guide, for embed mode, sandbox limits and the required poster.

`voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` searches supported asset libraries; `voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` saves under `assets/<source>/<id>/` with a receipt and a source/licence line in `CREDITS`. Tell the user when assets come from Poly Haven.

## Asset Sources

For licences, receipts and credits of third-party assets, and where free game art, icons, palettes, plugins and animations come from.

- Each grabbed asset gets a receipt `<asset-id>.json` beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`, `attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a line in the project's `CREDITS`: title, author, source URL, licence.

- `voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` searches Poly Haven (CC0 textures, HDRIs, models), ambientCG (CC0 materials, HDRIs), Kenney (CC0 packs), game-icons.net and Incompetech; `voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` saves under `assets/<source>/<id>/` with the receipt and the `CREDITS` line. Poly Haven asks that users are told its assets come from Poly Haven.

- Kenney (kenney.nl): CC0 whole packs (2D, 3D, UI, audio, textures); search matches pack names and categories only. Packs include `License.txt`.

- game-icons.net: CC BY 3.0 (a few authors CC0), credited per icon's author. Each SVG is a black square path under a white icon path; recolour or drop them via `fill`.

- Incompetech: Kevin MacLeod's music, CC BY 4.0 with his credit text; fetch single tracks only.

- Lospec: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json` returns name, author (sometimes empty; the palette page names the creator) and hex colours. Credit "<palette> by <author> (Lospec)".

- Godot Asset Library: keyless JSON at `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (without `godot_version` it returns nothing); `cost` holds the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`. Plugins and scripts, not art. The new Godot Asset Store (beta, no public API) is replacing it.

- OpenGameArt: no API. Search pages (`/art-search-advanced?keys=…`) only; robots.txt sets a 10 s crawl delay and disallows `/search/`. Licences (often several, including SA and GPL) and the attribution text are on each content page.

- Mixamo: Adobe's terms forbid access other than through its interface and any data mining, so the user downloads in their own browser; Voyager imports and rigs the FBX. Raw characters and animations are not redistributable.

- itch.io: no search API (every endpoint needs auth and covers your own account); tag pages have RSS (`itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-<tag>.xml`) without licences. Licences are free text per page; the user downloads, and pays where needed.
